# E021 -- Arthaus

## Metadata
- **Brand:** Arthaus
- **Industry:** Arts / Culture (likely an arts centre or cultural institution)
- **Year:** 2022
- **Region:** Spanish-speaking (Argentina, based on language and style)
- **Language:** Spanish
- **Source file:** arthaus-2022-pdf.pdf
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13, 20-21, 30-36, 45-46
- **Total pages:** 54 (landscape, 1920x1080, all-visual Illustrator export)

## Brand Strategy
- Core concept: "Una identidad flexible" (a flexible identity) -- the graphic identity is described as flexible and organic.
- "Flexible" because it uses few elements that transform and combine to convey sensations in each piece.
- "Organic" because it is built on rules justified by graphic and communication decisions.
- Two key terms: "variantes" (variants = different typographic uses per piece) and "variables" (variables = tone of communication choices: more informative/direct or more synthetic).
- Brand concept rooted in "contraste" (contrast) -- quoting about recognising the full range of human potential to weave a less arbitrary social fabric.

## Logo
- Wordmark "ARTHAUS" in an ultra-condensed, ultra-heavy typeface where letters are tightly packed, almost merging.
- The "H" in the centre acts as a visual anchor, often appearing as a solid black rectangle connecting the two halves "ART" and "AUS".
- Horizontal and vertical logo orientations, each with multiple accepted variations ("combinaciones aceptadas").
- All variations must maintain a consistent width measurement "X" (marked in green in the guidelines).
- Versions: positive (black on white), negative (white on black), on colour, on gradient, on image, and as a mask (logo used as a clipping mask revealing imagery beneath).
- Typographic style variation within the logo is permitted -- different letters can use different weights/styles of the Fixture typeface family.

## Typography
- **Primary typeface:** Fixture Ultra -- a hyper-condensed display sans-serif.
- Full weight range shown: Thin, Extralight, Light, Regular, Medium, Semibold, Bold, Extrabold, Black.
- The brand identity is dominated by typography at extreme scale -- type IS the graphic element.
- Mixed-weight typographic compositions are core to the identity: words within a single phrase can use different weights/sizes to create hierarchy and visual drama.

## Color
- **Primary colours:** Negro (Black, #000000, Pantone Black C) and Blanco (White, #FFFFFF, Pantone 11-0601 TCX).
- **Background:** Beige/cream as a warm neutral background (visible throughout the document).
- **Accent system:** Single accent colours used per piece -- vivid blue, orange/red, green, magenta/pink shown.
- Colour usage rules define three background modes:
  - Beige background: black figure + 1 colour accent
  - Black background: white figure + 1 colour accent
  - Colour background: black figure + beige accent
- Accent colours are deliberately saturated and high-contrast (cyan blue, neon green, hot pink, vivid red).

## Graphics / Illustration
- Typography at massive scale IS the graphic system -- no separate illustration language.
- "Elementos visuales" (visual elements) section shows type used as full-bleed graphic compositions.
- The logo itself functions as a graphic device when used as a mask or on imagery.
- Rotated/angled type compositions add dynamism.

## Photography
- Photography appears to be used through the logo-as-mask technique, with organic/fluid imagery (marbled, painterly textures) visible through letterforms.
- No standalone photography guidelines observed in sampled pages.

## Applications
- "Aplicaciones" section starts at page 44.
- Bold typographic posters using quotes about design/language/culture shown as application examples.
- All applications maintain the extreme typographic scale and contrast-driven aesthetic.

## Tone of Voice
- Intellectual, culturally engaged -- quotes about language creating reality, design being about function.
- Spanish-language throughout; the brand voice appears to be curatorial and philosophical.
- The dual "variantes/variables" system suggests communication can range from informative to poetic.

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- One of the most typographically radical brand identities in this collection -- the entire system is built on a single typeface at extreme scales.
- The logo variability system is unusually permissive: different accepted combinations of weight mixing within the wordmark itself.
- No conventional colour palette -- instead, a structural system (background/figure/accent) that allows any vivid colour.
- The document itself is a design artifact: 1920x1080 landscape slides, entirely visual, zero extractable text (all content is rendered as vector graphics).
- Strong Bauhaus/constructivist design heritage suggested by the name and aesthetic approach.

## Quality Score
4 / 5 -- Exceptional typographic system with clear rules for logo variation, colour usage structure, and a cohesive ultra-bold aesthetic. The flexibility framework (variantes + variables) is intellectually rigorous. Loses a point for limited photography direction and absence of detailed application templates beyond posters. The visual-only format, while stunning, makes the guidelines harder to reference as a practical tool.
